query: Help me understand the key points in this table — what should I concentrate on?

per_column.name: service_quality_assessment
per_column.rationale: A categorical service-quality axis is useful for grouping and comparison, and partly redundant with existing Staff Service / Overall Rating but adds a synthesized read. Groundedness is mostly sound for the clear cases, but sample 5 (an itinerary/scheduling complaint with no service description) is labeled 'poor' as a proxy for negativity rather than actual service evidence, a mild over-assertion.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_experience
per_column.rationale: Largely a restatement of the existing Seat Comfort column, reducing novel leverage, though a text-derived categorization can add nuance. NULL/Unknown for silent rows is correct behavior. However sample 3, whose text is about seat allocation/logistics not comfort, is labeled 'uncomfortable', an unwarranted inference.

per_column.name: food_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Overlaps with existing Food & Beverages column but a text-grounded categorical read is still usable. Values align with source: 'good/excellent' for praised meals, 'poor' for the syrupy-drink complaint, Unknown for silent rows — appropriate abstention.

per_column.name: operational_reliability
per_column.rationale: Genuinely new axis not present in original columns (delays, cancellations, punctuality) — high analytical value for identifying pain points. Grounding is mixed: on-time and landing samples are correct, but sample 5 (a route/aircraft swap, arguably a schedule change) is labeled 'cancellation', and the delay/cancellation distinctions are sometimes stronger than the text supports.

per_column.name: crew_professionalism
per_column.rationale: A finer-grained crew behavior axis beyond the numeric Staff Service score, useful for qualitative grouping. But grounding is weak on several rows: samples 3, 4 and 5 describe reservation/scheduling issues with friendly or unmentioned crew, yet all are labeled 'indifferent_lazy' — in sample 4 the text explicitly says 'friendly employees', so the label contradicts the source.

per_column.name: sentiment_direction
per_column.rationale: A bare positive/negative/mixed flag is largely redundant with the existing Recommended / Overall Rating fields and offers little new analytical leverage for this query. Values are well grounded in the review text.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively give useful qualitative axes for a 'what to concentrate on' review analysis, with operational_reliability and crew_professionalism providing the most genuine new leverage beyond the existing numeric ratings; seat and food columns partly restate original columns and sentiment_direction is a generic redundant flag. Groundedness is generally acceptable — NULL/Unknown abstention on silent rows is handled correctly — but the crew_professionalism and, to a lesser extent, service_quality_assessment columns over-assert negative labels on rows whose text is about logistics/reservations rather than crew, including one direct contradiction ('friendly employees' labeled indifferent_lazy).
